correctness.rationale: Exact flip-conservation equations rank 17 and the independent eight-ring equations agree on all 174 Boolean solutions. A complete eight-state labeled-graph subset construction, closed under all four pair-output letters, gives exactly 16 nonempty-subset-closed maps and a sharp 4/84/70 first-empty-depth distribution. Collision witnesses and explicit site-permutation maps distinguish the eight reversibles from the other eight surjective noninjective maps. Formal compactness transfers finite-word recognition to bilateral global surjectivity.

originality.rationale: The new 16-map global surjectivity classification and sharp three-pair obstruction are not equivalent to the preexisting broader reversibility classification. Eight of the sixteen are noninjective, so the new result is not deducible solely from the 2024 classification of reversible rules. Explicit published-finding corpus semantic queries returned no same 174/16/158 classification; relevant source full text and 2024 slide theorem were compared, with risks recorded.
residual_risks: The 2026 barriers-and-blocks paper was not available in full text; it could contain an implicit period-two image-language classification.
Unindexed historical numeric tables may encode the same 16-map surjectivity census; searched results cannot establish exclusive priority.
